raw: Okay so um I wanted to walk through where we are with the project. So the core is basically done, it's written in Rust, and um it handles the audio buffering and the provider adapters and the cleanup stage. And then there's the Mac app which is, uh, a menu bar app that does hold to talk. Now the thing I keep going back and forth on is whether we should do streaming transcription next or whether we should do the modes feature first. Because streaming is, you know, it's the biggest latency win, but modes is the thing that actually makes it feel different in Slack versus a terminal. And then separately there's the whole question of the iOS app, which um, is going to be hard because the keyboard extension can't touch the microphone at all, so we have to round trip through the container app.
why: The truncation bug. A long dictation must come back long, with every point intact.

raw: So the plan for next week is, um, we ship the streaming work on Monday, wait, actually Tuesday, because Monday is a holiday. And then Sarah is going to pick up the modes feature, and I think that's, uh, probably a two day job. After that we should have enough to do a real latency pass, and if the numbers look good we can start thinking about the iOS work, which honestly I think is going to be the hardest part of the whole quarter.
